BURSEVI:v10p317/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p317/r2.claim: The damned neither die to rest nor live a life that benefits them; then marks a further stage of severity, with existing between life and death worse than burning alone.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r2.anchor: حتى يستريح {ولا يحيى} حياة تنفعه كما يقال

BURSEVI:v10p317/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v10p317/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says they do not die and escape the pain of separation, nor live and attain the relief of union.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء لا يموت فيستريح من غم القطعية ولا يحيي فيصل إلى روح الوصلة

BURSEVI:v10p317/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r4.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v10p317/r4.claim: The Najmiyya reading says the self is not annihilated to end the veil's punishment and the heart cannot live by faith in the abode of recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r4.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : لا يموت نفسه بالكلية ليستريح من عقوبات الحجاب

BURSEVI:v10p317/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r5.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p317/r5.claim: Al-Qashani says the spirit cannot cease to exist, yet spiritual ruin deprives it of true life, so it is repeatedly revived for endless punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r5.anchor: وقال القاشاني : لا يموت لامتناع انعدامه ولا يحيي بالحقيقة لهلاكه الروحاني

BURSEVI:v10p317/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p317/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p317/r6.claim: The author adds that the damned remain in bodily and spiritual torment; true human life follows death to the self, unlike merely animal life.
BURSEVI:v10p317/r6.anchor: يقول الفقير لا يموت لأن الموت يذبح فلا موت ولا يحيى لأن المموم كالميت

QASHANI:87:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:13-15/r1.claim: The damned cannot cease to exist and are spiritually ruined, enduring torment and wishing for death; each time they burn and perish they are restored, so they are neither absolutely dead nor alive.
QASHANI:87:13-15/r1.anchor: بالحقيقة لهلاكه الروحاني أي: يتعذب دائما سرمدا في حالة يتمنى عندها الموت

SULAMI:v2p390#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p390#2/r1.claim: In Hell they neither die and gradually escape the grief of separation nor live and attain the comfort of union.
SULAMI:v2p390#2/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم يقول : قال ابن عطاء : لا يموت فيتدرج من غم القطيعة ولا يحيا فيصل إلى روح الوصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r3.claim: Thumma marks a higher rank of torment: burning is intensified because sensation continues without relief through death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r3.anchor: و ( ثم ) للتراخي الرتبي تدل على أن معطوفها متراخي الرتبة في الغرض المسوق له الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r4.claim: Not dying means not losing sensation; not living denies a pain-free life, preventing the audience from imagining a mild, nonfatal burning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r4.anchor: فمعنى { لا يموت } : لا يزول عنه الإحساس ، فإن الموت فقدان الإحساس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r5.claim: The negations form antithesis, not a conventional denial of two qualities to establish an intermediate state; alternatively, denied life can imply no escape.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p286/r5.anchor: وفي الآية محسن الطباق لأجل التضاد الظاهر بين { لا يموت } و { لا يحيى } .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r1.claim: The condemned person neither dies to find rest nor lives a life that benefits him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r1.anchor: ثم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى حياة تنفعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the person's soul lodges in the throat: it neither leaves to die nor returns to the body to live.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p91#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جرير تصير نفس أحدهم في حلقه فلا تخرج متفارقه فيموت ولا ترجع إلى موضعها من الجسم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r6.claim: The Prophet distinguishes permanent inhabitants of Hell, who neither live nor die, from sinners God mercies: intercessors retrieve them and they regrow like flood-carried seed in a river of life or Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها لا (2) يموتون ولا يحيون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r7.claim: A second version says sinful people are burned to charcoal, brought in groups after intercession, and grow again beside Paradise's rivers like seed in a flood's debris.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها، فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r9.claim: Thumma marks a further degree of severity: the state between life and death is worse than burning, since the damned neither die to rest nor live usefully.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p741/r9.anchor: لأن الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلى

MUQATIL:87:8-13/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r6.claim: The damned neither die to rest nor enjoy a good life; death reaches them everywhere, they burn repeatedly and are restored to punishment, with fire as clothing and food from their own flesh, and they never receive mercy, satiety, or relief.
MUQATIL:87:8-13/r6.anchor: لا يموت في النار فيستريح، ولا يحيا حياة طيبة، ولكنه في بلاء ما دام في النار يأتيه الموت من كل مكان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r1.claim: In Hell he neither dies and escapes torment nor lives a pleasurable life.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r1.anchor: فيستريح من العذاب ﴿ ولا يحيى ﴾ حياة يتلذذ بها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r2.claim: The word “then” indicates that the suspended state between life and death is even more dreadful than entering the Fire, so it comes later in severity.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#2/r2.anchor: وقيل ثم لأن الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه فى مراتب الشدة

QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r4.claim: The condemned neither die and find rest nor live a life of benefit; a poet describes a soul that neither dies nor lives enjoyably.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r4.anchor: أي لا يموت فيستريح من العذاب، ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه كما قال الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r5.claim: A report from Abu Saʿid says monotheist believers who enter Hell—the lesser fire, on al-Farraʾ’s view—burn and die until intercession for them; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r5.anchor: احترقوا فيها وماتوا إلى أن يشفع فيهم. خرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r6.claim: The wretched differ in degree; this warning concerns the most wretched, though others are also wretched at a lesser level.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:11-13/r6.anchor: وقيل: أهل الشقاء متفاوتون في شقائهم، هذا الوعيد للأشقى

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.claim: The Prophet fulfills his duty by reminding; people then diverge in response and outcome, and God deals with them according to how they receive the reminder.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:10/r1.anchor: فإذا نهض [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بهذا العبء فقد أدى ما عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:13/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:13/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:13/r1.claim: The damned person cannot die and find relief or live in safety and comfort; he endures eternal torment and longs for death.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:13/r1.anchor: الذي يتطلع صاحبه إلى الموت كما يتطلع إلى الأمنية الكبرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the damned neither die to find relief nor live a life of benefit; Arabs use this idiom for extreme suffering, as 35:36 does.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r1.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the soul reaches the throat but cannot leave in death or return to the body in life.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r2.anchor: نفس أحدهم في النار تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج فيموت

RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r3.claim: Then marks a further stage because this state is more terrible than entering the fire and is delayed in the progression of severity.
RAZI-FULL:v31p133#2/r3.anchor: هذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه في مراتب الشدة

SAMIN-DURR:87:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:13/r1.claim: Thumma marks a higher rank of severity rather than ordinary temporal delay.
SAMIN-DURR:87:13/r1.anchor: قوله: { ثم لا يموت }: " ثم " للتراخي بين الرتب في الشدة.

STUDYQURAN:87:12/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r3.claim: The Arabic idiom of neither living nor dying describes the experience of great trials.
STUDYQURAN:87:12/r3.anchor: In Arabic, to say that one neither lives nor dies is to indicate that one is suffering great trials

TAB-FULL:v24p318/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p318/r1.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p318/r1.claim: Another explanation invokes an Arabic idiom for a person in severe distress: he is neither alive nor dead.
TAB-FULL:v24p318/r1.anchor: لأن العرب كانت إذا وصفت الرجل بوقوع في شدة شديدة، قالوا: لا هو حي، ولا هو ميت،

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r9.claim: The denial of both death and life means no lasting escape: punishment would otherwise end either with death or with a change to blessed, comfortable life.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r9.anchor: نفي النجاة نفيا مؤبدا فإن النجاة بمعنى انقطاع العذاب بأحد أمرين إما بالموت

TABRISI:87:10-17/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r6.claim: The condemned neither die and rest nor have useful life; their existence becomes torment they wish would end.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r6.anchor: حياة ينتفع بها بل صارت حياته وبالا عليه

TABRISI:87:10-17/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r7.claim: Another explanation says they do not experience the breath of life.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r7.anchor: ولا يحيى أي ولا يجد روح الحياة

ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n8/r1.claim: The condemned person's inability to die or live follows from having kept away from divine reminders, as in 74:28–29.
ASAD-NOTES:87:9#n8/r1.anchor: in consequence of having remained aloof from the divine reminder

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p443/r8.claim: The damned do not die and find relief, but they also do not live a life that benefits them.

WAHIDI-QT:87:13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:13/r1.claim: In Hell he neither dies and rests from punishment nor lives with life's spirit.
WAHIDI-QT:87:13/r1.anchor: { ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى } لا يموت فيها موتا يستريح به من العذاب ولا يحيا حياة يجد فيها روح الحياة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r9.claim: In the Fire he neither dies to gain relief from torment nor lives a life with vitality.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r9.anchor: لا يموت فيها موتا يستريح به من العذاب، ولا يحيا حياة يجد فيها روح الحياة.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r16.claim: In hell he neither dies to escape torment nor has a life with pleasure or benefit that would make endurance meaningful; this is unsurpassable misery.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r16.anchor: Ölmez ki dünya azâbından kurtulduğu gibi kurtulsun, hayat yani zevk ve menfaati olan bir hayat da bulmaz ki çektiği azâbı ona vesile addederek sabr u tahammül etsin.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r17.claim: This fate is much worse than pasture turning to black coal refuse, and explains the outcome of those who shun admonition.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r17.anchor: mer‘aların kara bir gusâ olan kömüre çevrilmesinden çok büyük bir bedbahtlıktır. Ve işte va‘z u nasihat dinlemekten kaçınanların âkıbeti de budur.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r18.claim: Some exegetes hold that never dying in hell applies to disbelievers; sinful believers who enter it die, based on Muslim's report from Abu Sa'id.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r18.anchor: Demişlerdir ki cehennemde ölmemek kâfirlere mahsustur. Amma usât-ı mü’minînden cehenneme girenler orada öleceklerdir. Buna Müslim’in Ebû Sa‘îd’den rivayet ettiği şu hadis ile istidlâl eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r19.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r19.claim: The report says hell's permanent inhabitants neither die nor live, but God kills sinful people touched by the fire; after they become charcoal, intercession brings them to Paradise, where they grow when watered.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r19.anchor: Buna Müslim’in Ebû Sa‘îd’den rivayet ettiği şu hadis ile istidlâl eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r20.claim: For disbelievers, not dying or living follows the two deaths and two lives mentioned in 40:11, after resurrection for punishment.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r20.anchor: iki hayat ile azab için ba‘s olunduktan sonra demektir ki

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r21.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r21.claim: Others take the wording about neither dying nor living as a metaphor for enduring misery under the severity of torment.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r21.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir ki “ne ölmek ne de dirilmek” tâbiri şiddet-i azâb ile ebedî sürünmekten kinayedir.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:13:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:13:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:13:anmerkung/r1.claim: The claim that the damned cannot die in Hell is a Quranic topos: Q 20:74 repeats the wording, and Paret notes related formulations at Q 35:36, 43:77, and 69:27.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:13:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Hinweis, dass die Verdammten in der Hölle nicht sterben können, ist im Koran ein Topos

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza again addresses the messenger: he first praises God, perhaps with close followers, then speaks to a wider audience with an admonition that makes verse 6’s revelation public in purpose.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz beginnt wie das erste mit einem Aufruf an den Verkünder

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.claim: Verses 10–11 contrast good and bad responses to proclamation; verse 11 expands the bad response with a conventional warning of Hell, balanced by the promise to the good in verses 14–15.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Auf den das zweite Gesätz einleitenden Aufruf folgt in V. 10.11 eine Antithese

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The passage forms a chiasm: the responses of good and bad in verses 10–11 correspond to their fates in verses 12–15, as in Q 92:5–11 and 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Zusammen mit der an den Guten gerichteten Verheißung V. 14.15 ergibt sich eine chiastische Struktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.claim: The statement that the condemned neither die nor live conveys eternal, horrific punishment: they persist, but their suffering is no positive form of life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:9/r6.anchor: Cehennemdekiler ölmezler, yaşarlar; ancak çektikleri dikkate alındığında bunun olumlu anlamıyla yaşamak olmayacağı da muhakkaktır

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r1.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live a life that benefits them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r1.anchor: ثم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى أي حياة تنفعه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r2.claim: One reported explanation traps the soul in the throat, unable to leave and die or return to the body and live.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r2.anchor: وقيل إن روح أحجدهم تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج فيموت ولا ترجع إلى موضعها من الجسد فيحيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r3.claim: That explanation still needs qualification such as complete life, and remains open to objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r3.anchor: وهو غير غني عن التقييد بنحو حياة كاملة على أنه بعد لا يخلو عن بحث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r4.claim: Here thumma marks rank: this condition is worse than simply being burned in the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r4.anchor: وثم للتراخي في الرتبة فإنهذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من نفس المصلي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r5.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r5.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests the wording figuratively means that the damned do not escape punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r5.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن يكون هذا الكلام كناية عن عدم النجاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r6.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r6.claim: On that figurative reading, deliverance would require an abode in which a worker both dies and lives.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r6.anchor: لأن النجاة عن العذاب إنما يكون بالعمل في دار يموت فيها العامل ويحيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r7.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r7.claim: He argues the more fitting wording for the literal reading would say they are neither dead nor alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r7.anchor: والنظم أقرب إلى هذا المعنى كيف واللائق بالمعنى السابق ثم لا يكون ميتا فيها ولا حيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r8.claim: The literal reading fits the actual wording, which also preserves the verse endings; the proposed figurative rationale is unclear.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنه لائق به مع تضمنه رعاية الفواصل وكذا في توجيه كون ما ذكر كناية عن عدم النجاة خفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r9.claim: The wording can describe someone trapped in continuing hardship, signaling their permanence there; rank-based thumma is apt because eternal punishment is worse than entering and burning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r9.anchor: وقع في شدة واستمرفيها فلا يبعد أن يكون فيه إشارة إلى خلودهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r10.claim: The claim that no one dies in Hell applies specifically to disbelievers; sinful believers who enter it die there.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r10.anchor: عدم الموت في النار على ما صرح به غير واحد مخصوص بالكفرة وأما عصاة المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r11.claim: Muslim reports from the Prophet that Hell's permanent inhabitants neither die nor live, while sinful monotheists are killed, later interceded for, and brought to the Garden.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r11.anchor: بما أخرجه مسلم عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r12.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r12.claim: In the report, the rescued emerge like charcoal, are placed by Garden rivers, and grow like seeds carried by a flood.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r12.anchor: فجيء بهم ضبائر ضبائر فبثوا على أنهار الجنة ثم قيل يا أهل الجنة أفيضوا عليهم من الماء فينبتون نبات الحبة في حميل السيل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r13.speaker: ابن رجب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r13.claim: Ibn Rajab takes the report to mean these believers truly die, with their souls separating from their bodies; the verbal noun reinforces this.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r13.anchor: قال الحافظ ابن رجب أنه يدل على أن هؤلاء يموتون حقيقة وتفارق أرواحهم أجسادهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r14.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from Abū Hurayra, raised to the Prophet, that the lowest Garden inhabitants include people God removes from Hell because they associated nothing with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r14.anchor: ما أخرجه البزار عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا أن أدنى أهل الجنة حظا أو نصيبا قوم يخرجهم الله تعالى من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r15.claim: The report says they are cast in the open, grow like plants, and regain their souls before asking God to turn their faces away from Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r15.anchor: فينبذون بالعراء فينبتون كما ينبت البقل حتى إذا دخلت الأرواح أجسادهم فيقولون ربنا كما أخرجتنا من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r16.claim: They first suffer the punishment their sins merit, then remain dead until intercession; delayed entry and confinement complete their punishment, as beating followed by prison would.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r16.anchor: وهذه الإماتة على ما اختاره غير واحد بعد أن يذوقوا ما يستحقونه من عذابها بحسب ذنوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r17.claim: Their dead confinement lasts until permission for intercession, completing their punishment in another form rather than leaving them alive without torment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r17.anchor: وإبقاؤهم فيها ميتين إلى أن يؤذن بالشفاعة لا يجابه تأخير دخولهم الجنة تلك المدة كان تتمة لعقوبتهم بنوع آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r18.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r18.claim: Al-Qurṭubī allows that they die upon entering Hell, with exclusion from Garden delights during confinement itself serving as punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r18.anchor: وقال القرطبي يجوز أن تكون إماتتهم عند إدخالهم فيها ويكون إدخالهم وصرف نعيم الجنة عنهم مدة كونهم فيها عقوبة لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r19.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r19.claim: Al-Qurṭubī also allows them to feel pain while dead, but says this is lighter than remaining alive in Hell; al-Ālūsī treats the proposal skeptically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r19.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا متألمين حالة موتهم نحو تألم الكافر بعد موته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r20.speaker: مطامح الأفهام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r20.claim: Another proposal reads the hadith's death as sleep, since sleep is called a kind of death because sensation ceases; the report describes God waking monotheists with that hour's torment when releasing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r20.anchor: وفي مطامح الأفهام يجوز أن يراد بالإماتة المذكورة وفي الحديث الإنامة وقد سمى الله تعالى النوم وفاة لأن فيه نوعا من عدم الحس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r21.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that the first account of the believers' death is the relied-upon explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p108#4/r21.anchor: والمعول عليه ما ذكرناه أولا والله تعالى أعلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p402/r1.claim: The people of the fire neither die and find relief nor live a life that benefits them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r1.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live a life that benefits them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r1.claim: The word then marks the great interval or degree between enduring the fire and the bewildering state between death and life, whose full severity only God knows.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r1.anchor: فأشار إلى ذلك بالتعبير بأداة التراخي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r2.claim: The damned neither die in the fire, however long it lasts, nor live a beneficial life because they were not purified, believed, or prayed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r2.anchor: حياة تنفعه لأنه ما تزكى فلا صدق ولا صلى

ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r1.claim: The damned person neither dies to rest nor lives a pleasant life.
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r1.anchor: { ثم لا يموت } : فيستريح ،   { ولا يحيى } حياة هنيئة

ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r2.claim: Thumma signals gradation in severity: suspension between life and death is more dreadful than burning in the fire.
ABUHAYYAN:87:13/r2.anchor: وجيء بثم المقتضية للتراخي إيذاناً بتفاوت مراتب الشدة

ALUSI:87:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r1.claim: Those in the Fire do not die and thereby find relief.
ALUSI:87:13/r1.anchor: فيستريح { وَلاَ يحيى } أي حياة تنفعه

ALUSI:87:13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r2.claim: They do not have a life that benefits them.
ALUSI:87:13/r2.anchor: أي حياة تنفعه وقيل إن روح أحدهم تصير في حلقه

ALUSI:87:13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:13/r3.claim: One view says their souls remain in their throats, neither leaving to die nor returning to the body to live; al-Ālūsī says it needs an unsupported qualification and remains debatable.
ALUSI:87:13/r3.anchor: وقيل إن روح أحدهم تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج فيموت ولا ترجع إلى موضعها

ALUSI:87:13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r4.claim: Thumma marks a rise in degree: this condition is more terrible than merely entering and burning in the Fire.
ALUSI:87:13/r4.anchor: وثم للتراخي في الرتبة فإن هذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من نفس الصلى

ALUSI:87:13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r5.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:87:13/r5.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests this is a figure for not being saved, since salvation comes through deeds in earthly life, where a person dies and lives.
ALUSI:87:13/r5.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن يكون هذا الكلام كناية عن عدم النجاة لأن النجاة عن العذاب

ALUSI:87:13/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r6.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:87:13/r6.claim: He argues that the wording would more aptly say neither dead nor alive; al-Ālūsī rejects the objection and says the actual wording suits that meaning and preserves the rhyme.
ALUSI:87:13/r6.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن يكون هذا الكلام كناية عن عدم النجاة لأن النجاة عن العذاب

ALUSI:87:13/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r7.claim: The phrase can describe someone trapped in lasting hardship, implying enduring punishment; the rank progression makes eternal residence in the greater Fire worse than entering and burning in it.
ALUSI:87:13/r7.anchor: وقد يقال إن مثل ذلك لكم يقال لمن وقع في شدة واستمر فيها

ALUSI:87:13/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r8.claim: The statement that people do not die in Hell applies to unbelievers; sinful believers who enter it do die there.
ALUSI:87:13/r8.anchor: واعلم إن عدم الموت في النار على ما صرح به غير واحد مخصوص بالكفرة

ALUSI:87:13/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:13/r9.claim: Muslim reports from Abū Saʿīd that permanent inhabitants of Hell neither die nor live, but sinful monotheists are made to die like charcoal, then intercession brings them to Paradise's rivers, where they grow like flood-borne seed.
ALUSI:87:13/r9.anchor: ما أخرجه مسلم عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «( أما أهل النار الذين

ALUSI:87:13/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r10.speaker: ابن رجب
ALUSI:87:13/r10.claim: Ibn Rajab says this proves literal death with souls separated from bodies; the Prophet's emphatic made them die a death strengthens the point.
ALUSI:87:13/r10.anchor: قال الحافظ ابن رجب أنه يدل على أن هؤلاء يموتون حقيقة وتفارق أرواحهم أجسادهم

ALUSI:87:13/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:13/r11.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from Abū Hurayrah that people brought from Hell, though monotheists, are cast in the open and grow like plants until their souls enter their bodies.
ALUSI:87:13/r11.anchor: وأظهر منه ما أخرجه البزار عن أبي هريرة مرفوعاً أن أدنى أهل الجنة حظاً

ALUSI:87:13/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors literal death after sinners first suffer punishment in proportion to their sins; they remain dead until intercession, extending punishment by delaying Paradise and adding confinement without torment.
ALUSI:87:13/r12.anchor: وإبقاؤهم فيها ميتين إلى أن يؤذن بالشفاعة لا يجابه تأخير دخولهم الجنة تلك المدة

ALUSI:87:13/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:13/r13.claim: Remaining dead is not a period of unpunished life like the keepers; death may complete punishment or spare sinners the horror of seeing the Fire.
ALUSI:87:13/r13.anchor: ولم يبقوا أحيا فيها من غير عذاب كخزنتها إما ليكون أبعد عن أن يهولهم

ALUSI:87:13/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r14.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI:87:13/r14.claim: Al-Qurṭubī allows that sinners may die on entering Hell and be deprived of Paradise for a time, like prisoners confined without chains.
ALUSI:87:13/r14.anchor: وقال القرطبي يجوز أن تكون إماتتهم عند إدخالهم فيها ويكون ادخالهم وصرف نعيم الجنة

ALUSI:87:13/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r15.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI:87:13/r15.claim: Al-Qurṭubī also allows that they suffer while dead, like an unbeliever after death but before Resurrection, with less pain than if alive; al-Ālūsī is dismissive.
ALUSI:87:13/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا متألمين حالة موتهم نحو تألم الكافر بعد موته وقبل قيام الساعة

ALUSI:87:13/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:13/r16.speaker: مطامح الأفهام
ALUSI:87:13/r16.claim: Maṭāmiḥ al-Afhām suggests hadith death means sleep, since the Qurʾān calls sleep death when sensation is suspended; another Prophetic report says monotheists are killed in Hell and tormented when exit approaches.
ALUSI:87:13/r16.anchor: وفي مطامح الإفهام يجوز أن يراد بالإماتة المذكورة في الحديث الانامة

BAGHAWI:87:13/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:13/r1.claim: In the Fire he does not die and find relief, nor live a life that benefits him.
BAGHAWI:87:13/r1.anchor: { ثم لا يموت فيها } فيستريح ، { ولا يحيى } حياة تنفعه

BAYDAWI:87:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:13/r1.claim: The condemned person neither dies to find relief nor lives a beneficial life.
BAYDAWI:87:13/r1.anchor: ثم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى حياة تنفعه

BIQAI:87:13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:13/r1.claim: Thumma signals levels of the torment's extreme fluctuation between death and life whose height only God can know; no death recurs there, however long it lasts.
BIQAI:87:13/r1.anchor: فأشار إلى ذلك بالتعبير بأداة التراخي إعلاماً بأن مراتب هذه الشدة في التردد

BIQAI:87:13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:13/r2.claim: To prevent non-death from sounding like an extraordinary honor, Biqāʿī clarifies that the person has no beneficial life because he was not purified, truthful, or prayerful.
BIQAI:87:13/r2.anchor: أي حياة تنفعه لأنه ما تزكى فلا صدق ولا صلى

IBNASHUR:87:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated with “he enters the greatest Fire” as a second description of those who suffer there.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { يصلى النار الكبرى } فهي صلة ثانية

IBNASHUR:87:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r2.claim: Thumma marks a rise in rank of severity: torment is worse when burning brings neither relief through death nor release through life.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r2.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي تدل على أن معطوفها متراخي الرتبة

IBNASHUR:87:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r3.claim: “He does not die” means sensation does not cease; the extraordinary state strengthens the image of the punishment.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r3.anchor: لا يزول عنه الإحساس ، فإن الموت فقدان الإحساس

IBNASHUR:87:13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r4.claim: The added denial of life prevents hearers from mistaking survival of the burning for painless or comfortable life; it means no life free of pain.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r4.anchor: احتراس لدفع توهم أن يراد بنفي الموت عنهم أنهم استراحوا من العذاب

IBNASHUR:87:13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r5.claim: Alternatively, denying life is a metonym for denying escape, since burning ordinarily entails death while life entails not dying.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن نجعل نفي الحياة كناية عن نفي الخلاص بناء على أن لازم الإحراق الهلاك

IBNASHUR:87:13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r6.claim: He rejects reading the paired denials as merely a middle state between life and death, like “neither eastern nor western” or the saying about heat and cold.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r6.anchor: وليس هذا من قبيل نفي وصفين لإثبات حالةٍ وسطٍ بينَ حالتيهما

IBNASHUR:87:13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:13/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:13/r7.claim: The verse uses antithesis between dying and living.
IBNASHUR:87:13/r7.anchor: مُحسِّن الطباق لأجل التضاد الظاهر بين { لا يموت } و { لا يحيى }

IBNATIYYA:87:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r1.claim: The damned do not die a relieving death or live a pleasant life; they therefore remain alive in the Fire.
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r1.anchor: معناه : لا يموت فيها موتا مريحا ولا يحيا حياة هنية ، فهو لا محالة حي

IBNATIYYA:87:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r2.claim: A report says that sinners in the Fire are dead.
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r2.anchor: وقد ورد في خبر أن العصاة في النار موتى

IBNATIYYA:87:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:13/r3.claim: The report means death figuratively, like torpor, stillness, and lifelessness.

IBNKATHIR:87:11/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r1.claim: The wretched person avoids the reminder and enters the great Fire: he neither dies to rest nor lives a beneficial life, but remains conscious of painful punishment. This is echoed in 43:77 and 35:36.
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r1.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه ، بل هي مضرة عليه ؛ لأن بسببها يشعر ما يعاقب به من أليم العذاب

IBNKATHIR:87:11/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet distinguishing permanent inhabitants of Hell, who neither die nor live, from people shown mercy: intercession takes the latter to Paradise’s river, where they grow like flood-carried seed; the report compares their revival to a tree changing color. Ahmad transmits it, and Muslim gives a similar version.
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها

IBNKATHIR:87:11/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r3.claim: A second Abu Sa'id report says sinners are burned to charcoal, then released in groups through intercession and made to grow by the rivers of Paradise like seed in flood debris; Ahmad and Muslim transmit versions, and Ahmad also gives the route via al-Jariri.
IBNKATHIR:87:11/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها ، فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون

IBNKATHIR:87:13/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r1.claim: The wretched person avoids the reminder and enters the great Fire: he neither dies to rest nor lives a beneficial life, but remains conscious of painful punishment. This is echoed in 43:77 and 35:36.
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r1.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه ، بل هي مضرة عليه ؛ لأن بسببها يشعر ما يعاقب به من أليم العذاب

IBNKATHIR:87:13/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet distinguishing permanent inhabitants of Hell, who neither die nor live, from people shown mercy: intercession takes the latter to Paradise’s river, where they grow like flood-carried seed; the report compares their revival to a tree changing color. Ahmad transmits it, and Muslim gives a similar version.
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها

IBNKATHIR:87:13/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r3.claim: A second Abu Sa'id report says sinners are burned to charcoal, then released in groups through intercession and made to grow by the rivers of Paradise like seed in flood debris; Ahmad and Muslim transmit versions, and Ahmad also gives the route via al-Jariri.
IBNKATHIR:87:13/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها ، فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون

KASHSHAF:87:13/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:13/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:13/r1.claim: “Then” marks the state between life and death as a later, more severe degree of torment than burning itself.
KASHSHAF:87:13/r1.anchor: وقيل { ثُمَّ } لأنّ الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلي ، فهو متراخ عنه في مراتب الشدة

KASHSHAF:87:13/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:13/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:13/r2.claim: He neither dies and finds relief nor lives a life that benefits him.
KASHSHAF:87:13/r2.anchor: والمعنى : لا يموت فيستريح ، ولا يحيى حياة تنفعه .

MAWARDI:87:13/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:13/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:87:13/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the person neither dies nor experiences the breath of life.
MAWARDI:87:13/r1.anchor: أحدهما : لا يموت ولا يجد روح الحياة ، ذكره ابن عيسى

MAWARDI:87:13/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:13/r2.claim: Another is that the person is tormented without relief and gains no benefit from life; a poet’s line illustrates this state.
MAWARDI:87:13/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه يعذب لا يستريح ولا ينتفع بالحياة ، كما قال الشاعر

NASAFI:87:13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:13/r1.claim: In Hell the person does not die and find relief from punishment.
NASAFI:87:13/r1.anchor: فيستريح من العذاب { وَلاَ يحيى } حياة يتلذذ بها

NASAFI:87:13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:13/r2.claim: Nor does the person live a life that brings pleasure.

NASAFI:87:13/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:13/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:87:13/r3.claim: “Then” marks a later degree of severity: being suspended between life and death is more dreadful than burning.
NASAFI:87:13/r3.anchor: وقيل : «ثم » لأن الترجح بين الحياة والموت أفظع من الصلي

QURTUBI:87:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:13/r1.claim: He will not die and thereby find relief from torment, nor will he live a life that benefits him.
QURTUBI:87:13/r1.anchor: " ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى " أي لا يموت فيستريح من العذاب

QURTUBI:87:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:13/r2.claim: A cited poetic line uses the same paradox for a soul that neither dies to end its suffering nor lives a life with any taste.
QURTUBI:87:13/r2.anchor: ألا ما لنفسٍ لا تموتُ فينقضي

QURTUBI:87:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:13/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI:87:13/r3.claim: Muslim transmits from Abū Saʿīd that monotheist believers who enter Hell, described by al-Farrāʾ as the lesser fire, burn and die there until intercession is made for them.
QURTUBI:87:13/r3.anchor: حديث أبي سعيد الخدري ، وأن الموحدين من المؤمنين إذا دخلوا جهنم

QURTUBI:87:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:13/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:13/r4.claim: Another view says the wretched differ in degree: this severe threat concerns the most wretched, while others do not reach that rank.
QURTUBI:87:13/r4.anchor: وقيل : أهل الشقاء متفاوتون في شقائهم ، هذا الوعيد للأشقى

RAZI:87:13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:13/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the damned neither die and find relief nor live a beneficial life; Arabs describe severe misery as being neither alive nor dead.
RAZI:87:13/r1.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

RAZI:87:13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:13/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the soul remains caught in the throat in Hell: it cannot leave and cause death or return to the body and restore life.
RAZI:87:13/r2.anchor: أن نفس أحدهم في النار تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج

RAZI:87:13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:13/r3.claim: Thumma marks this state as delayed because it is more dreadful and severe than entering the Fire.
RAZI:87:13/r3.anchor: لأن هذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه في مراتب الشدة

TAB:87:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:13/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:13/r1.claim: In the great Fire, a person's soul reaches the throat but neither leaves so that he dies nor returns to his body so that he lives.
TAB:87:13/r1.anchor: وذلك أن نفس أحدهم تصير فيها في حلقه

TAB:87:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:13/r2.speaker: قيل
TAB:87:13/r2.claim: An alternative explanation is that the person neither dies and finds relief nor lives a life that benefits him.
TAB:87:13/r2.anchor: لا يموت فيها فيستريح ،   ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

TAB:87:13/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:13/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:13/r3.claim: Others say this follows an Arab idiom for someone in dire distress: he is neither alive nor dead.
TAB:87:13/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون :  قيل ذلك ،   لأن العرب كانت إذا وصفت الرجل بوقوع في شدة شديدة

ITQAN:v3p208#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p208#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p208#3/r1.claim: A thing may be denied entirely because its defining quality or benefit is absent: Hell's inmates neither die a full death nor live a wholesome, useful life.
ITQAN:v3p208#3/r1.anchor: فنفى عنه الموت لأنه ليس بموت صريح ونفى عنه الحياة لأنها ليست بحياة طيبة ولا نافعة

BURHAN:v3p395/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p395/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p395/r2.claim: The damned are denied death because theirs is not real death, and denied life because it is neither good nor beneficial life.
BURHAN:v3p395/r2.anchor: فنفي عنه الموت لأنه ليس بموت صريح ونفى عنه الحياة لأنها ليست بحياة طيبة ولا نافعة

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r1.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live a beneficial life; their continued life only lets them feel painful punishment and torment.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r1.anchor: أي : لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه ، بل هي مضرة عليه

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r2.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet’s distinction: permanent inhabitants neither die nor live, while people God wills to show mercy die in the Fire, are taken by intercessors, and grow again like flood-carried seed in a river of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r3.claim: A second report from Abū Saʿīd says sinners are killed by the Fire until they become charcoal, then taken in groups and made to sprout beside the rivers of Paradise like flood-borne seed.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها ، فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون ، ولكن أناس

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim transmits a similar Abū Saʿīd report through Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal and Shuʿba.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r4.anchor: ورواه مسلم في حديث بشر بن المفضل

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r5.claim: A further report from Abū Saʿīd distinguishes those God will not remove from Hell from sinners He will remove after making them charcoal and restoring them by Paradise’s rivers.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إن أهل النار الذين لا يريد الله إخراجهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir links the claim that the damned remain to 43:77, where they ask Mālik to end their lives and are told they will remain.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r6.anchor: وقد قال الله إخبارا عن أهل النار : { وَنَادَوْا يَامَالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ مَاكِثُونَ }

IBNKATHIR:87:12/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r7.claim: He also cites 35:36: the Fire’s punishment is not ended by death and is not lightened for its inhabitants.
IBNKATHIR:87:12/r7.anchor: وقال تعالى : { لا يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا وَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ عَذَابِهَا }

NAHHAS:v5p205/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r18.claim: One view says the people of Hell have souls trapped in their throats, neither leaving so they die nor returning to their bodies so they live.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r18.anchor: نفوس أهل النار في حلوقهم لا تخرج فيموتوا ولا ترجع إلى مواضعها

NAHHAS:v5p205/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r19.claim: Another view says they do not die and find relief, nor live a life that benefits them.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r19.anchor: لا يموتون فيستريحوا ولا يحيون حياة ينتفعون بها

NAHHAS:v5p205/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r20.claim: The phrase is also an Arabic idiom for extreme distress, when someone is neither alive nor dead.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r20.anchor: من قول العرب إذا كان في شدة شديدة ليس بحي ولا ميت

ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r6.claim: The people of Hell neither die to escape punishment nor enjoy the vitality of life.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r6.anchor: لا يموت موتا يستريح به من العذاب، ولا يحيا حياة يجد معها روح الحياة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.claim: The Prophet should not pursue the obdurate or force the message: he is to remind when useful, while the fearful heed it and the wretched evade it and face their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r1.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is directed not to go after the stubborn and the obdurate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r6.claim: The verses distinguish those who heed the warning from those who evade it; their rejection reflects their own condition, not a flaw in the message or preacher.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.claim: Evaders treat this life as all that exists and fear no Hereafter; they face eternal Fire, neither living nor dying, and will wish in vain for death.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r1.anchor: They regard this life to be all that there is.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.claim: The succeeding sūrah al-Ghāshiyah elaborates the same warning; its great torment and this passage's great Fire refer to the same punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p279/r3.anchor: Both refer to the same thing in slightly different styles

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r4.claim: The damned neither die to rest nor live pleasantly; thumma signals the added severity of remaining between life and death after burning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r4.anchor: ثم لا يموت: فيستريح، ولا يحيى حياة هنيئة وجيء بثم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.claim: The pure and fearful heed the reminder, while the wretched prefer worldly life and disregard the eternal one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r4.anchor: يتذكر به أهل النفوس الزكية الذين يخشون ربهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r8.claim: Not dying and not living means no relieving death and no pleasant life; the condemned remain alive, though a report calls sinners in Hell dead metaphorically.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r8.anchor: لا يموت فيها موتا مريحا، ولا يحيى حياة هنية فهو لا محالة حي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r9.claim: The report that sinners are dead in Hell is figurative, describing a state like dormancy, stillness, or languishing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470/r9.anchor: وأراه على التشبيه لأنه كالسبات والركود والهمول فجعله موتا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says those destined to remain in Hell neither die nor live; those God will remove are made charcoal, then emerge in groups and sprout after contact with Paradise’s rivers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r1.anchor: إن أهل النار الذين يريد الله إخراجهم يميتهم فيها إماتة، حتى يصيروا فحما، ثم يخرجون ضبائر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links the report to verses saying Hell’s inhabitants are not killed and their torment is not eased.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p380#2/r2.anchor: {لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها} [فاطر:36] إلى غير ذلك من الآيات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r21.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r21.claim: One view says they neither die nor experience the breath of life; another says they suffer without relief or benefit from life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r21.anchor: لا يموت ولا يجد روح الحياة , ذكره ابن عيسى . الثاني : أنه يعذب لا يستريح ولا ينتفع بالحياة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p254/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p254/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p254/r1.claim: An anonymous poetic line depicts a soul that cannot die and end its torment, yet cannot live a life with any savor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p254/r1.anchor: ألا ما لنفس لا تموت فينقضي … عناها ولا تحيا حياة لها طعم .

THALABI:v10p184/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p184/r9.claim: The wretched enters the greatest Fire, with no death for relief and no beneficial life.
THALABI:v10p184/r9.anchor: ثم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى أي حياة تنفعه

THALABI:v10p184#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
THALABI:v10p184#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads this spiritually: no rest from separation and no life of union.
THALABI:v10p184#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطا: لا يحيى! فيستريح عن القطيعة ولا يحيى فيصل
